claim.quote: Here we report the first high-statistics measurement, to our knowledge, of the ν̄μp → μ⁺p n cross-section from the hydrogen atom, using the plastic scintillator target of the MINERvA experiment, extracting FA from free proton targets and measuring the nucleon axial charge radius, rA, to be 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.

date.note: Published in Nature (London), Vol. 614, Issue 7946, February 2023.
date.quote: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering

key_value_text.quote: measuring the nucleon axial charge radius, rA, to be 0.73 ± 0.17 fm
key_value_text.value: Nucleon axial charge radius rA = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm, extracted from the first high-statistics ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section measurement on free (hydrogen) protons

name: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering

summary.plain: MINERvA measured, for the first time with high precision, how an antineutrino bounces off a bare proton (rather than one bound inside a heavier nucleus), pinning down the proton's 'axial' size to 0.73 femtometres.
summary.technical: First high-statistics measurement of the ν̄μp→μ⁺n cross-section on free (hydrogen) protons in the MINERvA plastic-scintillator target, avoiding the nuclear-correction uncertainties of deuterium-based extractions; yields the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q^2) and axial charge radius r_A = 0.73 ± 0.17 fm.

title: Measurement of the axial vector form factor from antineutrino–proton scattering
why_it_matters: The axial form factor sets the normalization for quasielastic neutrino-nucleon scattering, a dominant interaction channel used by oscillation experiments (MINOS, NOvA, DUNE) to reconstruct neutrino energy; a free-proton measurement removes a major source of nuclear-model uncertainty from that calibration.
